chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from Al-Hasan, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'When you see the crescent, break your fast and testify to it with just men from the Muslims. If you do not see the crescent except from the middle or end of the day, then
Complete the fasting until the night
And if it is obscured from you, then count thirty [days] and then break your fast.
ai.seo_question: What are the Shia rulings for determining the start of Ramadan based on moon sighting?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the Ahl al-Bayt chain in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, establishes the practical methodology for lunar calendar calculation, emphasizing the role of just witnesses ('udul) in validating the crescent sighting. It provides specific legal contingencies for late-day sightings and cloudy weather, reflecting the Shia emphasis on empirical observation combined with fixed thirty-day periods to ensure communal unity in worship.
